name: Linfield

adjustments.evidence: Repeated sectarian/discriminatory sanctions: UEFA fined the club EUR 10,000 for racist and/or discriminatory supporter behaviour (plus EUR 2,000 fireworks) and a suspended stand closure after the July 2025 Champions League qualifier v Shelbourne (anti-Catholic chants reported); Irish FA fined GBP 4,000 in Dec 2023 for sectarian chanting ('Billy Boys') at Larne and Cliftonville and a racist comment at a home game v Loughgall. Older: missiles at Celtic players (2017), sectarian-chant fines (2014), counted half. Behaviour continues.

evidence.C: Largest support in the Irish League (about 2,900 league average in 2021-22, double the league average; bigger for Big Two derbies and Europe). Loud, loyal following and strong away support. Home is Windsor Park (club owns the land since 1905; rebuilt 2016, 18,400, managed by the IFA as the national stadium), so a large modern bowl that is rarely full for club games.
evidence.V: Historically Protestant/unionist support base; sectarian chanting is a recurring sanction issue (Irish FA 2023, UEFA 2025). Club statements and manager Healy condemn sectarianism and racism; anti-sectarian and anti-racism programmes (FIFA commended 2006); charity shirt partner Cancer Focus NI; a women's team (Linfield Women) in the NI Women's Premiership. Bet McLean was sleeve/shorts sponsor through at least 2023-24 (current status unverified); new 2026-27 front-of-shirt sponsor is a wine merchant.
evidence.H: Founded 1886; world-record haul of national league titles (57) and 44 Irish Cups; seven-trophy 1961-62 season; Northern Ireland's defining club, Windsor Park the national team's home. Also carries the 1948 Belfast Celtic Boxing Day riot in its history.
evidence.O: Members-owned club. Board (chairman Roy McGivern) has said it will not sell a controlling stake but would consider minority outside investment (up to 49% per 2024 reports) and is in talks with several parties; nothing announced as of Oct 2026.
evidence.T: David Healy (Northern Ireland's record goalscorer) manager since Oct 2015, 11 seasons and 6 league titles: a defining coach and club icon. Settled core squad; won 2025-26 League Cup but finished 4th.

flags: Racism -6 is a judgement on sectarian chanting: Millwall -8 and Valencia -5 are the nearest club peers. Kevin's Ulster heritage (Northern Ireland national team bonus) does not apply to clubs.
Outside investment talks (minority stake) ongoing; if a deal is announced, R2 applies (Ownership -1 for PE/multi-club, +1 for a respected local investor).
Betting sponsor status for 2026-27 unverified (Bet McLean sleeve deal last confirmed 2023-24); if still on the kit, Values -0.5 more.
R3 coach: Healy 10+ full seasons, credited in T.

name: Derry City

adjustments.evidence: Spending well beyond the club's own income, funded by chairman Philip O'Doherty (Irish Times 2026 preview: 'big-spending Derry City'); he also paid for a GBP 3m North Stand and hybrid pitch at the council-owned Brandywell.

April 2024 v Shamrock Rovers: flare and missiles thrown into the away section from outside the ground, game stopped, PSNI vehicles attacked; suspended partial closure and fines, accepted by the club. 2022 UEFA charges (pitch invasion, objects thrown, crowd disturbance) at the CSKA Sofia qualifier, counted half.

evidence.C: Brandywell (about 3,700, now the Ryan McBride Brandywell Stadium) regularly sells out, average about 2,900-3,200 in 2022-24; noisy, city-wide support and a strong away following across the border. Loyalty: survived 13 years without senior football (1972-85) and the 2009 expulsion and re-formation.
evidence.V: Cross-border club from a nationalist city playing in the Republic's league; strong local identity without sanctioned sectarianism. Community standing around the late captain Ryan McBride; women's team (Derry City Women) in the NI Women's Premiership; local youth pathway. No betting shirt sponsor found. Values pulled down slightly by crowd incidents (2022, 2024).
evidence.H: Founded 1928; 1965 Irish League title and European Cup run; forced out of the Irish League in 1972 by the Troubles, joined the League of Ireland in 1985, 1989 treble; 2 league titles in the LOI, 6 FAI Cups (latest 2022). Expelled in 2009 over unofficial contracts, re-formed and kept its history.
evidence.O: Run and funded by local billionaire chairman Philip O'Doherty (Derry-born engineering founder) for about a decade; invests in the ground and squad, no fan protests. Benefactor dependence and spending beyond income handled in the overspend adjustment.
evidence.T: Coach churn: Ruaidhri Higgins (2021-Dec 2024), Tiernan Lynch (Jan 2025, sacked 5 Aug 2026 with the side sixth), director of football Mark Connolly interim. Big-budget recruited squad rather than a stable homegrown core.

flags: Ownership: Wikipedia's infobox still says 'supporter owned'; in practice O'Doherty is chairman and principal funder. Verify the company structure if O matters.
R3: two permanent coaches plus an interim in the last 3 seasons, so no churn hit by the letter; T already lowered for instability.
Violence -2 is borderline (2024 missiles came from outside the ground); Kevin may prefer 0.

name: Shamrock Rovers

adjustments.evidence: Dermot Desmond, Celtic's majority shareholder, owns 25% (since 2019); Rovers is a minority secondary holding, not a feeder, but fans have voiced 'Celtic offshoot' fears. Minor stake: -4 x 0.75.

evidence.C: Largest support in the League of Ireland at Tallaght Stadium (council-owned, about 10,000, home since 2009); active ultras and a strong away following. Loyalty through the 1987 sale of Milltown and two homeless decades; supporters' 400 Club rescued the club from examinership in 2005.
evidence.V: Strong academy pathway into the first team and to England (Bazunu, Kenny, many U-21 internationals); women's team in the Women's Premier Division; community programmes. Lowered: NetBet is the men's first-team sleeve sponsor ('responsible gambling partner', into 2026), criticised in the league; earlier betting partners Paddy Power, BoyleSports, 888sport.
evidence.H: Ireland's most successful club: record league titles (22 including 2025) and FAI Cups (26); 1980s four-in-a-row; first Irish club in a UEFA group stage (2022 Conference League), knockout play-off 2024-25, league phase 2025-26.
evidence.O: Shamrock Rovers Members Club owns 50% and elects four directors; Ray Wilson 25%, Dermot Desmond 25%. Shareholders' agreement amended so members cannot fall below 50%. Public friction in 2025 (Desmond letter criticising member directors, chairman reappointment not ratified).
evidence.T: Stephen Bradley head coach since 2016, ten seasons, five league titles: the defining coach (already credited, no extra R3 hit). Long-serving core (Roberto Lopes, Graham Burke, Jack Byrne), good bond with fans, front-foot possession style.

flags: Bradley was named a leading candidate for the Hibernian job in early Oct 2026; if he leaves, T drops by about 1.
Multiclub -3: Desmond's stake is minority and Rovers is not a feeder; Kevin may prefer 0 since the members hold 50% and a blocking position.
No betting shirt sponsor on the front, but the NetBet sleeve counts in full under the sportsbook rule.

name: Bohemians

evidence.C: Dalymount Park (1901, 'the home of Irish football') sells out most home games at about 4,500; loud, young, well-organised support with tifo and a large away following. Loyal through years of financial crisis (near-collapse around 2010-13, saved by members).
evidence.V: Openly progressive identity: Refugees Welcome kits, Bob Marley and Fontaines D.C. shirts with proceeds to charity, Palestine solidarity; 2026 shirt sponsor is the band Kneecap with a share of sales to a club-linked charity. Women's team in the Women's Premier Division, prison and community outreach programmes, affordable tickets. No betting sponsor found.
evidence.H: Founded 1890, one of Ireland's oldest clubs; 11 league titles and 7 FAI Cups, amateur until 1969, two titles in the 2000s; Dalymount hosted the national team for decades. Major national significance, modest beyond Ireland.
evidence.O: Member-owned (one member, one vote); members elect the board. Ground sold to Dublin City Council (2015), which is rebuilding Dalymount (EUR 63m, about 8,000 seats) with Bohs as tenant.
evidence.T: Alan Reynolds head coach since late 2023; Keith Long era (2016-22) built the current identity. Mid-table side in 2024, 4th in 2025; good player-fan bond, fairly high squad churn.

flags: Dalymount rebuild: Bohs leave for a temporary ground in 2027 (dates conflicting: end of 2026 season or first half of 2027), back in a new 8,000-seat stadium on the same site around end-2028. A welcomed upgrade on the same site: R2 Culture +1 could apply, but the move-out is temporary and the old ground's character is lost; left at no change. Kevin to decide.
Kneecap sponsorship (2026) is political: an Irish-language rap group whose member's 2025 terror charge in the UK was thrown out; counted as part of the progressive identity, not against Values.
Pyrotechnics: Bohs away fans banned for one match in 2024 after a flare struck a St Pat's player during an anti-FAI protest; no violence adjustment (isolated, club condemned it).
